label: early z: original-phase steps 2-4 after a z among the first three tokens
explanation: Fires during the original (input) phase at steps 2-4 (peak at t=3, 99.6% of mass in the original phase) when the letter z appeared earlier among the first three original tokens (positions 0-2). It is a short-lived z-in-prefix detector: rate is 16x baseline when the token two steps back is z, and 9.5x when the previous token is z. Magnitude is largest when z is the first token, and largest of all for runs like z z z (top examples reach the max at t=3 right after z z z), usually decaying over the next 1-2 steps. It is weak or near zero when z appears at position 2 and only fires at t=3-4, then fades. It does not fire at t=0-1, on the z token itself at t<2, after step ~5, on z appearing later in the sequence (position >=3), or in the copy phase (only a weak echo at the delimiter step). Current input token identity barely matters (about 1x lift for every token). Residual errors: steps where the activation has already decayed to zero, and weak tails at t=5.

issues: Precision falls off along the lag axis inside the predicate. z@0 by step: t=2 1.00, t=3 0.96, t=4 0.46. z@1: t=2 0.77, t=3 0.99, t=4 0.85. z@2: t=3 0.69, t=4 0.77. So the feature is better described as 'z 1-3 steps back, while z was in the first three positions' than as a fixed t=2-4 window. Most false positives are the z@0, t=4 cell (13.8k predicted steps, 46% precision). Restricting that cell to sequences that have a second z gives test F1 0.8445, against 0.8437 for the original predicate. Precision goes up (0.859) but recall drops (0.830), so it is no real improvement.

Undercovered weak activations. The predicate covers only 61% of the lowest activation quartile. The misses are 12% of active steps but only 3.8% of activation mass. They are spread over t=5-6 tails (t=5 with z@2 or z@3: precision 0.17) and weak firing after a z at position 3 (precision 0.13, 0.9% of mass). The label's 'does not fire on a z at position 3 or later' is mostly true, but there is a faint low-precision tail.

The 'weak echo at the delimiter' wording is slightly off. In top examples with L=4-5 after 'z z z', <DEL> reaches 0.5 of max. That is the normal t=3-4 continuation landing on the delimiter step, not a separate echo. It covers only 865 steps (0.4% of mass), and adding phase<=1 lowers test F1 to 0.821.

Other claims check out. Original-phase mass share is 0.996. Firing is zero at t=0-1 and peaks at t=3. Lift is 15.9x when the token two steps back is z and 9.5x when the previous token is z. The current input token gives about 1x lift. The maximum is at t=3 after 'z z z' and fades over the next 1-2 steps. z first carries 46% of mass and z@1 37%. Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.812, R 0.879, F1 0.844, mass recall 0.962.
Minor: there is a slight lift for prev/prev2 == '1' (1.3-1.5x). It is negligible and not systematic enough to matter.
